extracted.intended_audience: printers, stationers, Company of Stationers officers, and parliamentary enforcement officers in 17th‑century England
extracted.subtask_description: Parliamentary and Company of Stationers orders (1643–1646) and associated court decrees governing who may print, how printing is licensed, employment/ apprenticeship rules in the printing trades, search/seizure and penalties, and obligations about reserved copies for libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship number limits for printers
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified maximum numbers of apprentices depending on the printer's rank: every Matter‑Printer who is or has been Matter/Upper Warden may have three apprentices; every Matter‑Printer of the Livery may have two; every Master‑printer of the Yeomanry may have one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apprenticeship limits cannot be circumvented by partnership, binding at scriveners, or other devices; if an apprentice 'run or be put away' the master may not take a replacement unless the departed apprentice's name be erased from the Hall‑book and never admitted again, under pain of being disabled from using a press and other punishments 'as by this Court, or the high Commission Court respectively' may require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to employ free journeymen printers
rubrics_metrics.description: Master and Wardens of the Company of Stationers must take special care that all journeymen printers who are free of the Company and of honest behaviour and able in trade are set to work and employed within the Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unemployed journeyman shall repair to the Master and Wardens; they (with one or two master printers) shall first offer his service to the master under whom he served his apprenticeship if living and allowed, or to another master the Wardens deem fit. Every master printer is bound to employ one journeyman who is so offered, and more if need requires; penalties (including imprisonment) may follow for failure to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation and penalties for refusing to assist unemployed journeymen
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Master and Wardens or any of them refuse or neglect to go with an honest and sufficient journeyman seeking their assistance to find employment, they shall suffer imprisonment and other punishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a master has more employment than he can discharge with his apprentice(s) he may require the help of unemployed journeyman(s); if such journeymen refuse or neglect accepted employment, they too shall suffer imprisonment and other penalties 'as this Court shall think fit.'

rubrics_metrics.name: University printers exempt from apprenticeship caps but limited in labour movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Printers of the Universities are not restrained by the apprenticeship-number rules; they may take as many apprentices for service in printing at the University as they themselves think fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided that University printers must employ all their own journeymen within the University and not suffer those journeymen to seek employment with London printers (except to supply extraordinary workmen when London printers desire them), under penalty imposed by the Chancellor of the relevant University.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only trade freemen or apprentices may work at the press or case
rubrics_metrics.description: No master‑printer shall employ any persons to work at the case, the press, or other printing tasks except such men or apprentices to the trade or mystery of printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation carries penalty of being disabled forever to keep or use any press or printing house, and such further punishment as the Court or High Commission may impose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unauthorized persons setting up or working at presses
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person not an allowed printer who presumes to set up any press for printing, or to work at any such press, or to compose letters to be wrought by such press, is guilty of a penal offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offenders shall be set in the pillory, whipped through the city of London, and suffer such other punishments as the Court or High Commission shall order, upon complaint or proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to search for secret/unlicensed printing and to seize presses/materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The Master and Wardens of the Company of Stationers, or any two licensed master‑printers appointed by the Lord Archbishop of Canterbury or the Lord Bishop of London, shall have authority to take assistance and search houses/shops (especially printing houses), view printing operations, call for licences, and if unlicensed seize so much as is printed and the several offenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Those seized may be brought before the bishops so that 'they or either of them may take such further order therein as shall appertain to justice.' The authorized searchers may act 'at what time they shall think fit' and may seize presses, letters, nuts, spindles and other materialls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searchers may seize books suspected of anti‑Church or anti‑State content
rubrics_metrics.description: If searchers find books or parts of books they suspect to contain matter contrary to the doctrine and discipline of the Church of England or against the State and Government, they may seize them and bring them to the Lord Archbishop of Canterbury or the Lord Bishop of London.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bishops shall then take such further course as they deem fit; seizure based on suspicion is authorized by the Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and regulation of founders of letters (typefounders)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be four founders of letters for printing allowed and no more; the Court names four persons to hold that office for the time being, and the bishops may appoint other high commissioners to supply places as they fall void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No person not allowed as a Founder shall 'found or cast letters for printing'; upon complaint and proof such offenders shall suffer such punishment as the Court or High Commission thinks fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship limits for matter‑founders (typefounders)
rubrics_metrics.description: No matter‑founder shall keep more than two apprentices at one time, nor take a replacement apprentice when one runs away unless the departed's name is erased from the Hall‑book and they are never admitted again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations carry punishment including being disabled from the practice and other penalties by the Court or High Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journeyman‑founders to be employed and idle journeymen compelled to work
rubrics_metrics.description: All journeyman‑founders shall be employed by the matter‑founders of the trade, and idle journeymen shall be compelled to work in like manner and under like penalties as specified for journeyman‑printers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement parallels the employment and penalty regime applied elsewhere in these Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labour restrictions in the cutting/founding of letters
rubrics_metrics.description: No matter‑founder shall employ any person in work belonging to the cutting or founding of letters except freemen or apprentices to that trade (with the sole exception of one boy allowed to pull off metal knots after casting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using persons not bound to the trade is punishable by being forever disabled to use or exercise that art and additional penalties as the Court or High Commission may impose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑conviction sureties, disposal of forfeitures, and burning of seditious books
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons convicted of offences under these decrees must, before discharge and beyond fines, be bound with good sureties never after to transgress in the same kind; forfeitures (except seditious/ schismatic books which are to be burned and except forfeitures already granted by Letters Patent) shall be divided and disposed of as the High Commission Court finds fit, with one moiety to the King.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prescribes both personal preventive measures (sureties) and the financial/physical disposition of seized/forfeited materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importation landing point restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: No merchant, master or owner of any ship or vessel, or any person, shall land or put ashore any imported books or parts of books within the realm except only in the Port of the City of London.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is to ensure books may be viewed; officers of His Majesty's Ports are required to take notice and enforce the rule; violation incurs forfeiture to the owner(s) of the copies and further punishment as thought fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to reserve and send one copy to University library (Bodleian/Oxford)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every printer shall reserve one book of every sort that is newly printed or reprinted with additions and, before any public venting of the book, bring it to the Common Hall of the Company of Stationers to be delivered to the officer to be sent to the University library at Oxford.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reserve and deliver such copy is punishable by imprisonment and such further order/direction as this Court or the High Commission Court think fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parliamentary control: only Houses may authorize printing of their Orders and licences for other works
rubrics_metrics.description: No Order or Declaration of either House of Parliament shall be printed except by order of one or both Houses. No book, pamphlet, paper, or part thereof shall be printed, bound or put to sale unless first approved and licensed under the hands of persons appointed by one or both Houses for licensing, entered in the Register Book of the Company of Stationers, and the printer must put his name thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also forbids printing or reprinting of works granted to the Company of Stationers for maintenance of their poor without licence/consent of the Master, Wardens and Assistants; importation of such works is likewise forbidden; penalties include forfeiture and other punishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement powers granted to Company officers, Parliamentary officers, and Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The Master and Wardens of the Company, the Gentleman Usher of the House of Peers, the Sergeant of the Commons House and their deputies, and persons appointed by the Committee for Examinations are authorized and required to make diligent search for unlicensed presses and scandalous/unlicensed papers, seize and carry away presses, letters, nuts, spindles and other materials to the Common Hall for defacement, and to apprehend authors, printers and others implicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seized materials remain at Common Hall until disposal by the Houses; apprehended persons are to be brought before either House or the Committee to receive further punishment; no one committed shall be released until persons employed in apprehension are satisfied for pains and charges; all justices, captains, officers and constables are required to assist and may break open doors in case of opposition. The Order must be printed and published so contemners are inexcusable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of the Committee for Examinations specifically about scandalous pamphlets
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee for Examinations or any four of them may appoint persons to search any house where presses are suspected of printing scandalous and lying pamphlets, demolish and take away such presses and their materials, seize nuts and spindles, and bring master‑printers and workmen before the Committee; they may commit to prison any persons who contrive, vend, publish, or refuse search regarding such pamphlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons committed for these offences shall not be released until those employed in their apprehension are satisfied for pains and charges; all justices and officers are required to assist in apprehension and searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printer's name and author's consent requirement; certification of offenders
rubrics_metrics.description: Printers must print their own name on works and must not print or reprint anything without the name and consent of the author; if any printer prints or reprints without the author's name and consent, proceedings shall be taken against the printer and author and their names certified to the House.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule protects proprietorship and prevents anonymous/unlicensed reproduction; offenders are to be proceeded against and certified to Parliament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and publicity of enforcement orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders for regulating printing, seizing presses and punishing offenders are to be forthwith printed and published so that notice may be taken and contemners be left inexcusable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly requires immediate printing and publication of the Orders to facilitate enforcement and awareness.
